data.title: Minimum Meeting Rooms Required
data.solution:
import sys
import math

# Auto-generated code below aims at helping you parse
# the standard input according to the problem statement.

n = int(input())

start_list = []
end_list = []

for i in range(n):
    start, end = [int(j) for j in input().split()]
    start_list.append(start)
    end_list.append(end)

start_list.sort()
end_list.sort()

i = 0
j = 0
rooms = 0
max_rooms = 0

while i < n:
    if start_list[i] < end_list[j]:
        rooms += 1
        max_rooms = max(max_rooms, rooms)
        i += 1
    else:
        rooms -= 1
        j += 1

# Write an answer using print
# To debug: print("Debug messages...", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)

print(max_rooms)
data.statement:
You are given the start and end times of N meetings. Each meeting requires one room for its entire duration.

Your task is to determine the minimum number of rooms required so that all meetings can be scheduled without any overlap in the same room.

A room can be reused for another meeting if the previous meeting ends at or before the next meeting starts.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

You are given the start and end times of N meetings. Each meeting requires one room for its entire duration.

Your task is to determine the minimum number of rooms required so that all meetings can be scheduled without any overlap in the same room.

A room can be reused for another meeting if the previous meeting ends at or before the next meeting starts.
Input
Line 1: An integer N for the number of meetings.

Next N lines: Two space-separated integers start and end representing the start time and end time of a meeting.
Output
Line 1 : A single integer representing the minimum number of rooms required to schedule all meetings.
Constraints
1 <= N <= 100
0 <= start< end <= 10^9
Example
Input
3
0 30
5 10
15 20
Output
2
